rv.q: Theater for a New Audience’s “Remember This: The Lesson of Jan Karski,” originally produced by the Laboratory for Global Performance and Politics at Georgetown University, is a dignified and affecting solo show.
Strathairn is exceptionally able to breathe electricity into it.
'Remember This' immerses us much more powerfully in the experience of Karski himself. The culminating scenes are particularly sobering.
It is not only a remarkable performance, it is also an impressive reconstruction of another man’s character and deeds.

In this moving, immersive tribute to one man’s efforts to expose the truth, Karski’s adjurations live on. His message does not age: that we must listen and act in the presence of inhumanity and unimaginable evil.
The clear directive placed right in the title of Remember This might be exactly what the world needs.
All hail to him for putting his immense talent in the service of Karski's life.
The only clear lesson in this play about a man who tried to stop the Holocaust is that we need plays like this, in order to remember.
Strathairn’s considerable acting skills bring this true-life story alive for generations to remember long after Karski’s death.
Remember This: The Lesson of Jan Karski, is Strathairn at his most dynamic, stirring and unforgettable.
Nevertheless, Remember Me lends credence to those who view history as the best drama.
Theater David Strathairn proves bearing witness can be heroic in 'Remember This' (Off Broadway review) Date: September 15, 2022.

cn.t: Strathairn delivers a powerful, riveting solo performance as Polish Holocaust witness Jan Karski, though the overwhelming cascade of atrocities can leave audiences emotionally numb in this vital, timely historical drama.
